title: What Makes a Cuttlefish Change Color in 0.2 Seconds?

scenes.text: A sea creature flips its skin palette in just 0.2 seconds!
Special pigment cells called chromatophores expand or contract with muscle control.
scenes.label: CHROMATOPHORES ACTION

scenes.text: Iridophores reflect light, adding shimmering blues and greens that shift instantly.
scenes.label: IRIDOPHORES REFLECT

scenes.text: Neural signals travel at lightning speed, coordinating all cells for a seamless transition.
scenes.label: NEURAL SPEED COORDINATION
